title: Part 3 — Conversation 1: renegotiating a maintenance contract
instructionsVi: Ở mục tiêu 800, Part 3 có câu hỏi về hàm ý của một câu nói cụ thể, không chỉ hỏi sự việc.
promptEn: Listen to the conversation and answer questions 32 through 34.

transcript.speaker: M
transcript.text: Thanks for seeing me. We'd like to extend the maintenance contract, but your quote is well above what we budgeted.

transcript.speaker: W
transcript.text: What figure did you have in mind?

transcript.speaker: M
transcript.text: About ninety thousand a year. Your quote is a hundred and twelve.

transcript.speaker: W
transcript.text: I can't reach ninety at the current service level. That would mean losing the four-hour response guarantee, and I don't think you'd want that.

transcript.speaker: M
transcript.text: No — the response time is the reason we're with you.

transcript.speaker: W
transcript.text: Then let's look at scope instead. You have quarterly inspections at all fourteen sites. Half of them have had no issues in three years. Move those to twice a year and I can get to ninety-eight.

transcript.speaker: M
transcript.text: Ninety-eight I could defend internally. Send me the list of sites you'd reclassify and I'll take it to the finance committee.

questions.prompt: 32. What is the main obstacle?

options.text: The response guarantee is too slow.
The quoted price exceeds the budget.

questions.explanationVi: 'your quote is well above what we budgeted' — 112 so với 90 nghìn.

questions.prompt: 33. What does the woman mean when she says, 'I don't think you'd want that'?

options.text: The client should reduce the number of sites.
She is refusing to negotiate further.
The client would reject a slower response time.
She doubts the client can pay.

questions.explanationVi: Câu trước nói giá 90 nghìn đồng nghĩa mất bảo đảm phản hồi 4 giờ; người đàn ông xác nhận ngay sau đó.

questions.prompt: 34. What will the man do next?

options.text: Take a revised proposal to a committee

questions.explanationVi: 'I'll take it to the finance committee' sau khi nhận danh sách các điểm được phân loại lại.

title: Part 3 — Conversation 2: an audit finding
format: TOEIC Listening — Part 3 · Conversation 2, ba người nói (câu 35–37)
instructionsVi: Ba người nói, có nói giảm mang tính mỉa. Nghĩa thật thường ngược với nghĩa đen của câu chữ.
promptEn: Listen to the conversation among three speakers and answer questions 35 through 37.

transcript.speaker: W1
transcript.text: The auditors have flagged the approvals process. Fourteen purchases over the threshold went through without a second signature.

transcript.speaker: M
transcript.text: Fourteen out of how many? Fourteen out of nine hundred is a different conversation from fourteen out of twenty.

transcript.speaker: W1
transcript.text: Fourteen out of thirty-one.

transcript.speaker: M
transcript.text: Ah. Well, that's certainly a number.

transcript.speaker: W2
transcript.text: In fairness, the second-signature rule only came in during March and nobody was told. I found out because I read the intranet, which I don't think anyone else does.

transcript.speaker: W1
transcript.text: That's a reasonable point, and it changes what we recommend. If the rule wasn't communicated, the finding is about our rollout, not about people ignoring controls.

transcript.speaker: M
transcript.text: I'd still want the fourteen reviewed individually before we conclude that.

questions.prompt: 35. What does the man mean by 'that's certainly a number'?

options.text: He believes the audit was inaccurate.
He thinks the proportion is alarmingly high.

questions.explanationVi: Nói giảm mang tính mỉa. Ông ta vừa lập luận rằng tỉ lệ mới quan trọng; 14 trên 31 là gần một nửa.

questions.prompt: 36. What point does the second woman make?

options.text: The auditors reviewed the wrong period.
Staff were not informed when the rule changed.

questions.explanationVi: 'the second-signature rule only came in during March and nobody was told'.

questions.prompt: 37. Why does the man still want the cases reviewed?

options.text: In case some are irregular for other reasons
To prepare a report for the intranet

questions.explanationVi: 'I'd still want the fourteen reviewed individually before we conclude that' — tức trước khi kết luận nguyên nhân chỉ là do phổ biến kém.

title: Part 3 — Conversation 3: a warranty claim
instructionsVi: Nghe rồi trả lời 3 câu. Có một điều khoản kèm ngoại lệ; câu hỏi nhắm đúng vào ngoại lệ.
promptEn: Listen to the conversation and answer questions 38 through 40.

transcript.speaker: W
transcript.text: I'm calling about a compressor that failed. It's two years and one month old, so I assume we're outside warranty.

transcript.speaker: M
transcript.text: Standard cover is twenty-four months, yes. But do you hold an annual service plan?

transcript.speaker: W
transcript.text: We do — both services completed on time.

transcript.speaker: M
transcript.text: Then you're on the extended term, which is thirty-six months. You're still covered.

transcript.speaker: W
transcript.text: There's one complication. The chamber reached forty-six degrees overnight, and I know there's an exclusion above forty.

transcript.speaker: M
transcript.text: There is. But why did it reach forty-six?

transcript.speaker: W
transcript.text: The thermostat stopped regulating. It's your unit — supplied with the compressor.

transcript.speaker: M
transcript.text: Then the exclusion doesn't apply. There's a clause covering excursions caused by our own equipment. Submit the claim and reference the thermostat.

questions.prompt: 38. Why is the unit still under warranty?

options.text: The fault was reported within 30 days.
The customer is a long-standing client.
The customer holds a service plan with all services completed.

questions.explanationVi: Gói bảo dưỡng năm kéo dài cover từ 24 lên 36 tháng, và cả hai lần bảo dưỡng đều hoàn thành.

questions.prompt: 39. Why does the temperature exclusion not apply?

options.text: 46 degrees is within the permitted range.
It was caused by the supplier's own thermostat.
The exclusion was removed last year.

questions.explanationVi: 'There's a clause covering excursions caused by our own equipment'.

questions.prompt: 40. What is the woman told to do?

options.text: Submit a claim referencing the thermostat
Wait for an engineer to call

questions.explanationVi: 'Submit the claim and reference the thermostat'.

title: Part 3 — Conversation 4: a hiring dilemma
instructionsVi: Nghe rồi trả lời 3 câu. Hai bên có quan điểm khác nhau và cùng thừa nhận điểm mạnh của phía kia.
promptEn: Listen to the conversation and answer questions 41 through 43.

transcript.speaker: M
transcript.text: We're down to two for the analyst role. Mensah has the stronger technical test; Vasquez interviews better.

transcript.speaker: W
transcript.text: How much stronger on the test?

transcript.speaker: M
transcript.text: Substantially. Ninety-one against sixty-eight.

transcript.speaker: W
transcript.text: That's not a small gap. My hesitation is that this role spends half its time explaining findings to people who don't want to hear them, and the test doesn't measure that at all.

transcript.speaker: M
transcript.text: Agreed. Though I'd rather teach communication to someone who can do the analysis than teach analysis to someone who can't.

transcript.speaker: W
transcript.text: That's fair. Let's offer Mensah, but I'd want a development plan for the presenting side written into the first six months.

questions.prompt: 41. What is the woman's concern about Ms Mensah?

options.text: Her technical score is too low.
She is unavailable for six months.
The test does not measure communication.

questions.explanationVi: 'this role spends half its time explaining findings… and the test doesn't measure that at all'.

questions.prompt: 42. What is the man's argument?

options.text: The interview matters more than the test.
Communication is easier to teach than analysis.

questions.explanationVi: 'I'd rather teach communication to someone who can do the analysis than teach analysis to someone who can't'.

questions.prompt: 43. What condition does the woman attach to the offer?

options.text: A development plan for presenting skills

questions.explanationVi: 'I'd want a development plan for the presenting side written into the first six months'.

title: Part 3 — Conversation 5: a data protection query
instructionsVi: Nghe rồi trả lời 3 câu. Người nói dùng nhiều điều kiện lồng nhau — bỏ một vế là chọn sai.
promptEn: Listen to the conversation and answer questions 44 through 46.

transcript.speaker: W
transcript.text: A former customer has asked us to delete everything we hold on them. Can we just do that?

transcript.speaker: M
transcript.text: Mostly. You delete the marketing records and anything you kept out of convenience.

transcript.speaker: W
transcript.text: And the transaction history?

transcript.speaker: M
transcript.text: That you keep. Tax law requires six years, and a deletion request doesn't override a statutory retention period.

transcript.speaker: W
transcript.text: Do I need to tell them that?

transcript.speaker: M
transcript.text: Yes, and that's the part people get wrong. You must respond within thirty days explaining exactly what you've deleted and what you've retained, and why. Silence is a breach even if the deletion itself was done correctly.

questions.prompt: 44. What must be deleted?

options.text: Marketing records and data kept for convenience

questions.explanationVi: 'You delete the marketing records and anything you kept out of convenience'.

questions.prompt: 45. Why is transaction history retained?

options.text: The customer did not ask for it.
It is stored on a separate system.
Tax law requires six years' retention.

questions.explanationVi: 'Tax law requires six years, and a deletion request doesn't override a statutory retention period'.

questions.prompt: 46. What does the man say people get wrong?

options.text: Failing to reply explaining what was kept and why
Charging a fee for the request

questions.explanationVi: 'Silence is a breach even if the deletion itself was done correctly'.

title: Part 3 — Conversation 6: a quality hold
format: TOEIC Listening — Part 3 · Conversation 6, ba người nói (câu 47–49)
instructionsVi: Ba người, có xung đột giữa hai bộ phận. Câu hỏi cuối hỏi phương án giải quyết thế bế tắc.
promptEn: Listen to the conversation among three speakers and answer questions 47 through 49.

transcript.speaker: W1
transcript.text: I've held four batches from line two. Same measurement failed on all four — about eleven thousand units.

transcript.speaker: M
transcript.text: Production says the line is within tolerance and we've got a shipping deadline on Friday.

transcript.speaker: W1
transcript.text: Our gauge was calibrated last month. I don't think the problem is on my side.

transcript.speaker: W2
transcript.text: So we have two instruments disagreeing and a deadline in three days. Arguing about whose gauge is right won't resolve it in time.

transcript.speaker: M
transcript.text: What would?

transcript.speaker: W2
transcript.text: Send thirty units to the external lab this afternoon. Result tomorrow morning, still inside the deadline, and neither side has to concede anything on trust.

transcript.speaker: W1
transcript.text: I'd accept that. The hold stays until the result comes back.

questions.prompt: 47. Why have the batches been held?
questions.explanationVi: 'Same measurement failed on all four'.

questions.prompt: 48. What does the second woman identify as the real obstacle?

options.text: Two instruments disagreeing with a deadline approaching

questions.explanationVi: 'we have two instruments disagreeing and a deadline in three days. Arguing about whose gauge is right won't resolve it in time'.

questions.prompt: 49. What solution is agreed?

options.text: Delaying the shipment by a week
Independent testing by an external lab

questions.explanationVi: 'Send thirty units to the external lab this afternoon… neither side has to concede anything on trust'.

title: Part 3 — Conversation 7: an unexpected resignation
instructionsVi: Nghe rồi trả lời 3 câu. Người nói liên hệ hai sự việc mà không nói thẳng kết luận — câu hỏi hàm ý nhắm vào đó.
promptEn: Listen to the conversation and answer questions 50 through 52.

transcript.speaker: M
transcript.text: Three of the night team resigned this week. All on the same day.

transcript.speaker: W
transcript.text: Same day? Did they say why?

transcript.speaker: M
transcript.text: All three mentioned the shift-swap system. They've been refused leave twice since it came in.

transcript.speaker: W
transcript.text: The system went live in March, didn't it. And this is the first cluster of resignations we've had on nights in two years.

transcript.speaker: M
transcript.text: I'll leave you to draw the obvious conclusion.

transcript.speaker: W
transcript.text: Right. I'll get agency cover for the immediate gap, but I want the automatic refusal rule suspended while we review it. Otherwise we lose the ones who stayed.

questions.prompt: 50. What reason did the leavers give?

options.text: The shift-swap system and refused leave

questions.explanationVi: 'All three mentioned the shift-swap system. They've been refused leave twice since it came in'.

questions.prompt: 51. What does the man imply by 'I'll leave you to draw the obvious conclusion'?

options.text: The resignations are unrelated to the system.
The new system is very likely the cause.
The night team is difficult to manage.

questions.explanationVi: Hai sự việc được đặt cạnh nhau — hệ thống mới từ tháng Ba và cụm nghỉ việc đầu tiên trong hai năm — rồi để người nghe tự nối.

questions.prompt: 52. What does the woman want to do about the underlying cause?

options.text: Suspend the automatic refusal rule during a review

questions.explanationVi: 'I want the automatic refusal rule suspended while we review it. Otherwise we lose the ones who stayed'.
